<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Reward and Credit Assignment</h2>

<section id="S6.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.1 </span>Three-hop examination</h3>

<div id="S6.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All chunks in a window are written before scoring. For each question, the harness retrieves a memory block from the written bank, the frozen answer model answers using only that block, and the frozen judge compares the answer with the reference and weighted rubric. This scores deployable bank behavior. Directly asking a judge whether retrieved text “contains the answer” would not test whether contradictory or stale memories cause an incorrect response.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.2 </span>Per-chunk recall reward</h3>

<div id="S6.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For chunk <math id="S6.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, let <math id="S6.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> be positive probes and <math id="S6.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> traps. With score <math id="S6.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{i}\in[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{i}\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
<table id="S6.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.E3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{prm}[t]=\frac{\sum_{i\in R_{t}}z_{i}+\sum_{j\in P_{t}}z_{j}}{|R_{t}|+|P_{t}|}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>prm</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></msub><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em">+</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></msub><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{prm}[t]=\frac{\sum_{i\in R_{t}}z_{i}+\sum_{j\in P_{t}}z_{j}}{|R_{t}|+|P_{t}|}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S6.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">“PRM” here means per-chunk recall reward, not a reward model over hidden reasoning steps. A chunk with no valid probes receives zero rather than one. Items lost to an answer or judge service failure leave the denominator; policy failures remain scoreable and receive low reward.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.3 </span>Attributed outcome reward</h3>

<div id="S6.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For outcome question <math id="S6.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math>, the judge returns <math id="S6.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{q}[t]\in[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{q}[t]\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>, the degree to which the answer recovered gold evidence introduced by chunk <math id="S6.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>. If <math id="S6.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> is the set of questions citing chunk <math id="S6.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
<table id="S6.E4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.E4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{orm}[t]=\frac{1}{|Q_{t}|}\sum_{q\in Q_{t}}c_{q}[t]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>orm</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></munder><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{orm}[t]=\frac{1}{|Q_{t}|}\sum_{q\in Q_{t}}c_{q}[t].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(4)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S6.SS3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Averaging prevents a chunk from receiving more weight merely because the annotator wrote more questions about it.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.4 </span>Bank-growth penalty</h3>

<div id="S6.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S6.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> be bank-token growth divided by input-chunk tokens. Each harness has a free-growth lower threshold <math id="S6.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{h}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{h}</annotation></semantics></math> and a full-penalty threshold <math id="S6.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u_{h}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u_{h}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S6.EGx2" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S6.Ex2"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S6.Ex2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle x_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle x_{t}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S6.Ex2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\mathrm{clip}\!\left(\frac{g_{t}-\ell_{h}}{u_{h}-\ell_{h}},\,0,\,1\right)," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:1.428em;" width="1.428em"><mi>clip</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>h</mi></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>h</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo>,</mo><mn> 0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn> 1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\mathrm{clip}\!\left(\frac{g_{t}-\ell_{h}}{u_{h}-\ell_{h}},\,0,\,1\right),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S6.E5"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S6.E5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathrm{pen}[t]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>pen</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathrm{pen}[t]</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S6.E5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\frac{e^{3x_{t}}-1}{e^{3}-1}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\frac{e^{3x_{t}}-1}{e^{3}-1}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S6.SS4.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Tokens are measured instead of entry count because a writer can grow a bank by lengthening existing records. Shrinking the bank is neither taxed nor directly rewarded. Figure <a href="#S4.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ 4.1 Why two stages ‣ 4 Two-Stage Training ‣ Hy-Memory-30B-A3B: Attributed Reinforcement Learning for Long-Term Memory Writing" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> labels this term Penalty.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.5 </span>Combined score</h3>

<div id="S6.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<table id="S6.EGx3" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S6.Ex3"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S6.Ex3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle s[t]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle s[t]</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S6.Ex3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=w_{\mathrm{prm}}\sum_{k\geq t}\gamma^{k-t}\,\mathrm{prm}[k]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>prm</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>≥</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></munder></mstyle><mrow><msup><mi>γ</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>prm</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=w_{\mathrm{prm}}\sum_{k\geq t}\gamma^{k-t}\,\mathrm{prm}[k]</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S6.E6"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S6.E6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\quad+w_{\mathrm{orm}}\,\mathrm{orm}[t]-w_{\mathrm{pen}}\,\mathrm{pen}[t]," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>orm</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>orm</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>pen</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>pen</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\quad+w_{\mathrm{orm}}\,\mathrm{orm}[t]-w_{\mathrm{pen}}\,\mathrm{pen}[t],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(6)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S6.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S6.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{\mathrm{prm}}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>prm</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{\mathrm{prm}}=1</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S6.SS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{\mathrm{orm}}=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>orm</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{\mathrm{orm}}=2</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S6.SS5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{\mathrm{pen}}=0.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>pen</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{\mathrm{pen}}=0.3</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S6.SS5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma=0</annotation></semantics></math>. Gold-fact ORM attribution handles delayed cross-chunk evidence, so <math id="S6.SS5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma=0</annotation></semantics></math> avoids broadcasting noisy future recall scores backward.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.6 </span>How this resolves sparse ORM</h3>

<div id="S6.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Probes give every chunk a local signal, so a sequence is not limited to a few terminal questions. Weighted rubrics with partial credit and distractors replace binary answer reward. Traps and the bank-growth penalty penalize over-storage. Gold facts attribute outcome evidence to evidence chunks instead of broadcasting one score. The answer model and judge are frozen, so reader improvements cannot hide writer defects. Continuous signals increase within-group resolution. Carrying the selected policy-written bank into the next window preserves cross-session effects. This is closer in spirit to process supervision than terminal-only RL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lightman et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, but the supervised unit is an externally verifiable bank consequence rather than a subjective reasoning step.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS7" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.7 </span>Chunk-level GRPO</h3>

<div id="S6.SS7.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">GRPO estimates a baseline from several samples without a separate value model <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shao et al., 2024</a>)</cite>. Standard GRPO scores each sampled trajectory once, normalizes that score within the group, and applies the resulting advantage to every token of the trajectory. A trajectory-level group is not appropriate here: all eight rollouts share the same bank only at chunk 0; after that, rollout <math id="S6.SS7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> observes the bank created by its own earlier actions, and a single trajectory score would again broadcast one judgment over all of its writes. We instead compute advantages per chunk, grouping by window, harness configuration, sequence, and chunk position:</p>
<table id="S6.E7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.E7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{i,t}=\frac{s_{i}[t]-\mu_{t}}{\sigma_{t}+\epsilon}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{i,t}=\frac{s_{i}[t]-\mu_{t}}{\sigma_{t}+\epsilon},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(7)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S6.SS7.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S6.SS7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S6.SS7.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> are the mean and standard deviation of <math id="S6.SS7.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{j}[t]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{j}[t]</annotation></semantics></math> over the chunk-level group <math id="S6.SS7.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The best rollout can therefore differ from chunk to chunk: rollout 1 may have the highest score at chunk 2 while rollout 3 is best at chunk 4, and each chunk’s writes are reinforced or suppressed according to their own column (Figure <a href="#S4.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ 4.1 Why two stages ‣ 4 Two-Stage Training ‣ Hy-Memory-30B-A3B: Attributed Reinforcement Learning for Long-Term Memory Writing" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS7.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS7.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Each rollout contributes one vote to the baseline for a chunk. If a multi-stage harness made three LLM calls for that chunk, all three segments receive the same advantage but do not count as three independent observations. Otherwise the policy could alter the baseline by changing its call count. Groups with fewer than two valid rollouts receive zero advantage.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS8" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.8 </span>Bank carry-forward</h3>

<div id="S6.SS8.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Bank selection is a separate, rollout-level decision. At the end of a window, the eight final banks are ranked by <math id="S6.SS8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{t}s[t]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>t</mi></msub><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{t}s[t]</annotation></semantics></math>. The winner becomes the initial state of the next window in that sequence; the others are discarded. If all candidates fail because of platform faults, the previous bank is reused. Bank state is checkpointed with model state.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS8.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS8.p2.1" class="ltx_p">An inherited error from an earlier optimizer step cannot receive retrospective gradient. Carrying imperfect policy-written banks is still preferable to teacher forcing with an ideal bank: deployment also requires the writer to operate on its own prior mistakes. An inherited error common to all candidates also tends to cancel in the group-relative baseline rather than being assigned to the current chunk.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S7" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">7 </span>Training System</h2>

<div id="S7.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each harness is packaged behind a common interface: <span id="S7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">bank_open</span>, <span id="S7.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">write</span>, <span id="S7.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">search</span>, <span id="S7.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">bank_stats</span>, and <span id="S7.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">bank_close</span>. The harness owns its native control flow. Harness-invoked LLM calls are routed to the policy endpoint and recorded at generation time with token ids, rollout log-probabilities, segment boundaries, and MoE routing. This follows the harnessed-agent-RL pattern in which the deploy-time loop is kept intact while model calls connect to a trainer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Luo et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. Retokenizing text after execution can diverge from the sampled stream, and recomputing rollout log-probabilities with the training engine destroys the intended importance ratio.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S7.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Stage 2 starts from the OPD model, on Hy3-30B-A3B (<math id="S7.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim</annotation></semantics></math>3B active parameters), using 16 nodes <math id="S7.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> 8 H20 GPUs (128 GPUs). A batch is 64 windows <math id="S7.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> 8 rollouts, or 512 trajectories. The objective is a PPO-style clipped surrogate with chunk-level GRPO advantages, aggregated as sequence mean then token mean, with no KL penalty. MoE routing from the rollout is replayed during training. The learning rate is <math id="S7.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5\mathrm{e}{-6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5\mathrm{e}{-6}</annotation></semantics></math>, constant. The context is 28,672 prompt tokens plus 4,096 response tokens. The resulting post-RL model is released and evaluated as Hy-Memory-30B-A3B. Model, optimizer, schedule, and selected banks are checkpointed every 10 steps during training.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S8" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">8 </span>Experiments</h2>

<section id="S8.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">8.1 </span>Evaluation principles</h3>

<div id="S8.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S8.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The evaluation changes only the memory writer. For each comparison, the harness version and prompts are fixed, retrieval configuration is fixed, and the answer model, judge, and other framework-side components are held fixed. Throughout this report, every reference to a DeepSeek Flash endpoint denotes <span id="S8.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">DeepSeek V4.1 Flash</span>. Decoding settings are matched where APIs permit, each writer builds its own bank from an empty state, and test examples and scoring rules are identical. This is necessary because memory quality is otherwise confounded with retrieval depth, reader capability, auxiliary-model capability, or a pre-existing bank.</p>
</div>
<section id="S8.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Sampled benchmark matrix.</h4>

<div id="S8.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S8.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For computational efficiency, every benchmark in the main four-harness matrix is evaluated on a fixed 20% subsample. The evaluated post-RL model is Hy-Memory-30B-A3B. Scores are deterministic outputs of the fixed evaluation pipeline; no missing judgment is imputed as zero. Each harness score is the equal-weight average of six metrics: LoCoMo Judge, LongMemEval, PersonaMem-v2, Travel SPS, Shopping PS, and Code Memory Bench (CMB). CMB is itself the equal-weight average of two repository QA evaluations. The overall score is the equal-weight average of the four harness scores.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S8.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">

</table>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 6: </span>Six-metric means on fixed 20% benchmark subsamples. The macro average weights the four harnesses equally.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S8.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S8.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Hy-Memory-30B-A3B ranks first on all four harnesses. Relative to Opus 5, it gains 0.60 points on Mem0, 0.02 on Hy-Memory, 0.01 on MemOS, and 2.86 on EverMemOS, for a macro-average gain of 0.87 points. Relative to DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, it gains 4.29 points on Mem0, 0.35 on Hy-Memory, 1.34 on MemOS, and 1.42 on EverMemOS, for a macro-average gain of 1.85 points. Relative to the Hy3-A3B base checkpoint, the macro average improves by 7.84 points. The 0.01–0.02 point margins on MemOS and Hy-Memory indicate parity with Opus 5 under this deterministic sampled evaluation, not a statistically resolved difference. The stronger evidence is the consistent ranking and the larger margin on the held-out framework.</p>
</div>
<div id="S8.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S8.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The six metrics stress different behaviors, so the average improvement does not require Hy-Memory-30B-A3B to win every column. Its strongest recurring gains are on Travel SPS and CMB. On the held-out EverMemOS harness, the gain is driven particularly by Travel SPS (+10.65 points) and CMB (+13.66 points). Appendix <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Detailed Benchmark Results ‣ Hy-Memory-30B-A3B: Attributed Reinforcement Learning for Long-Term Memory Writing" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a> reports all six benchmark scores for every model and harness.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S8.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">8.3 </span>OOD framework generalization</h3>

<div id="S8.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S8.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">EverMemOS is not part of OPD or RL training. It is included only at evaluation time as a held-out framework and is the strongest open-source community memory baseline in this evaluation. Hy-Memory-30B-A3B reaches 56.89, compared with 55.47 for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, 54.04 for Opus 5, and 52.30 for Hy3. This result separates model-level memory-writing skill from memorization of the training harness protocols.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S8.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">8.4 </span>Future ablations and audits</h3>

<div id="S8.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S8.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This report does not include controlled ablations of chunk-level versus window-level GRPO, gold-fact attribution versus broadcast ORM, positive probes versus probes plus traps, the bank-growth penalty, binary versus rubric-based rewards, RL initialization from OPD versus generic SFT, or single-harness versus mixed-harness training. We leave these comparisons to future work. Additional reward-data audits should measure human–judge agreement, sensitivity to the judge model and prompt, score distributions across synthetic answer types, separation between strong and weak memory writers, and the fraction of zero-variance rollout groups before and after reward decomposition.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S9" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">9 </span>Engineering Lessons: Silent Failures</h2>

<div id="S9.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S9.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Several failures looked healthy until an invariant was checked. A bank that did not persist across windows still left files on disk and produced nonzero rewards; the check is to reopen a checkpointed bank and verify a known record before training. A teacher that returned no top-<math id="S9.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> values still returned successful requests, but OPD gradients were zero; missing teacher fields must raise, and teacher-token coverage must be monitored. When the per-chunk mapping was absent, a fallback broadcast one score to every segment; missing chunk-to-segment mappings must raise. A configuration omitted from a hard-coded schedule still had valid artifacts on disk; schedule manifests must be audited against the declared harness set. String rules that graded semantics produced a plausible aggregate reward; semantic conditions belong in judge rubrics, not substring code. A “read all” that silently paginated made the bank entry count plateau at a default limit; pagination and token accounting must be tested explicitly. Failed writes checkpointed as empty were marked complete; platform faults must be retryable and excluded from denominators. Sandboxes that shared a trajectory identity completed requests attached to the wrong rollout; every request must validate bank and trajectory identity. Malformed output treated as an environment error made bad actions disappear from training; policy mistakes should remain valid low-reward trajectories.</p>
</div>
<div id="S9.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S9.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The governing rule is: a bad policy action must receive low reward; a platform failure must not be misrepresented as policy behavior.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S10" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">10 </span>Limitations and Future Work</h2>

<div id="S10.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S10.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Attribution is evidence-based rather than counterfactual: recovered gold facts do not prove that a specific write caused an answer. Credit is truncated across optimizer steps, so earlier-bank errors cannot receive retrospective gradient. One-vote grouping fixes the baseline, but multi-call chunks can still carry more loss mass. Rubric rewards reduce sparsity but require human-agreement and judge-sensitivity checks. The reward artifact covers Chat, Working, and Coding but not every long-term-memory workload; EverMemOS is only one held-out framework. The primary matrix uses deterministic 20% subsamples, so 0.01–0.02 point margins are not statistically significant; repeated training seeds remain future work. Finally, pooled scores can hide whether gains come from extraction, update, deletion, reconciliation, or retrieval-facing representation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S11" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">11 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S11.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S11.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Memory writing is a long-horizon control problem over an external state, not merely a summarization prompt. Hy-Memory-30B-A3B first learns to operate real memory harnesses through on-policy distillation, then optimizes the answerability and selectivity of the banks it creates through Memory RL. The central technical contribution is the reward interface: failure-driven probes make supervision dense, cross-chunk questions measure downstream utility, gold facts attribute that utility to source chunks, traps and growth penalties close the store-everything shortcut, and chunk-level GRPO compares actions at the correct decision boundary.</p>
</div>
<div id="S11.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S11.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Hy-Memory-30B-A3B ranks first on Mem0, Hy-Memory, MemOS, and held-out EverMemOS. On fixed 20% benchmark subsamples, it averages 55.49% across six metrics and four harnesses, ahead of Claude Opus 5 at 54.62%, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at 53.64%, and the Hy3-A3B base checkpoint at 47.66%. The OOD EverMemOS result provides the clearest margin over Opus 5 (+2.86 points). Together, these results support memory writing as a transferable model capability rather than a collection of framework-specific prompt heuristics.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="Sx1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section">Resource Availability</h2>

<div id="Sx1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="Sx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The Hy-Memory framework code and evaluation utilities are available at
<a href="https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/Hy-Memory" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/Hy-Memory</a>. The Hy-Memory-30B-A3B model weights, configuration, and model card are
available on Hugging Face at <a href="https://huggingface.co/tencent/Hy-Memory-30B-A3B" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://huggingface.co/tencent/Hy-Memory-30B-A3B</a>.</p>
</div>
</section>

<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Detailed Benchmark Results</h2>

<div id="A1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Tables <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Detailed Benchmark Results ‣ Hy-Memory-30B-A3B: Attributed Reinforcement Learning for Long-Term Memory Writing" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a>–<a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Detailed Benchmark Results ‣ Hy-Memory-30B-A3B: Attributed Reinforcement Learning for Long-Term Memory Writing" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a> report the six benchmark scores used to compute each harness mean in Table <a href="#S8.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ 8.2 Final cross-harness results ‣ 8 Experiments ‣ Hy-Memory-30B-A3B: Attributed Reinforcement Learning for Long-Term Memory Writing" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>. All scores use the same fixed 20% benchmark subsamples as the main evaluation. Hy-Memory-30B-A3B uses the post-RL model reported throughout this paper. Checkpoint identifiers are omitted.</p>

  <div class="keyboard-glossary">
    <h2>Instructions for reporting errors</h2>
    <p>We are continuing to improve HTML versions of papers, and your feedback helps enhance accessibility and mobile
      support. To report errors in the HTML that will help us improve conversion and rendering, choose any of the
      methods listed below:</p>
    <ul>
      <li>Click the "Report Issue" <span class="mobile-only">(<svg role="presentation"
            style="display: inline-block; vertical-align: middle; fill: var(--text-color);" aria-hidden="true"
            height="1em" viewBox="0 0 640 640">
            <path
              d="M224 160C224 107 267 64 320 64C373 64 416 107 416 160L416 163.6C416 179.3 403.3 192 387.6 192L252.5 192C236.8 192 224.1 179.3 224.1 163.6L224.1 160zM569.6 172.8C580.2 186.9 577.3 207 563.2 217.6L465.4 290.9C470.7 299.8 474.7 309.6 477.2 320L576 320C593.7 320 608 334.3 608 352C608 369.7 593.7 384 576 384L480 384L480 416C480 418.6 479.9 421.3 479.8 423.9L563.2 486.4C577.3 497 580.2 517.1 569.6 531.2C559 545.3 538.9 548.2 524.8 537.6L461.7 490.3C438.5 534.5 395.2 566.5 344 574.2L344 344C344 330.7 333.3 320 320 320C306.7 320 296 330.7 296 344L296 574.2C244.8 566.5 201.5 534.5 178.3 490.3L115.2 537.6C101.1 548.2 81 545.3 70.4 531.2C59.8 517.1 62.7 497 76.8 486.4L160.2 423.9C160.1 421.3 160 418.7 160 416L160 384L64 384C46.3 384 32 369.7 32 352C32 334.3 46.3 320 64 320L162.8 320C165.3 309.6 169.3 299.8 174.6 290.9L76.8 217.6C62.7 207 59.8 186.9 70.4 172.8C81 158.7 101.1 155.8 115.2 166.4L224 248C236.3 242.9 249.8 240 264 240L376 240C390.2 240 403.7 242.8 416 248L524.8 166.4C538.9 155.8 559 158.7 569.6 172.8z" />
          </svg>)</span> button, located in the page header.</li>
    </ul>
    <p><strong>Tip:</strong> You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.</p>
    <p>Our team has already identified <a class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/arXiv/html_feedback/issues"
        target="_blank">the following issues</a>. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we
      may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability
      should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for
      all.</p>
    <p>Have a free development cycle? Help support accessibility at arXiv! Our collaborators at LaTeXML maintain a <a
        class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/wiki/Porting-LaTeX-packages-for-LaTeXML"
        target="_blank">list of packages that need conversion</a>, and welcome <a class="ltx_ref"
        href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/issues" target="_blank">developer contributions</a>.</p>
  </div>
